sections.title: Intro
sections.prompt: This is live and there is no single right answer. We care about how you think. Ask us questions any time. If you're unsure, say so.

sections.title: Part 1: PR review
sections.prompt: Walk us through what you notice in the code, and what feedback you would give the member.
hints: What happens if this input is empty or unexpected?
Does this match how the rest of the repo handles it?
Which comment would you leave first for a newer member?
items: TBD: PR issue 2 (logic or validation bug)

sections.title: Part 2: Unfamiliar territory (scope, then design)
hints: Who uses this and what do they do with it?
Given your team and timeline, what ships first?
Where does the data come from and where does it live?
What happens if this step fails?
Anything about this data or the users you would handle carefully?

sections.title: Part 3: Project walkthrough
sections.prompt: Walk us through a project you built.
hints: Pick one request and trace it from start to finish.
items: One full data flow end to end
Where the design breaks under scale

sections.title: Part 4: Behavioral
sections.prompt: Younger, less experienced members will produce less than senior members. How will you ensure they feel ownership over the project?
items: A week before a deadline you realize the team won't finish everything. How do you decide what to cut, and who do you tell?
(If time) A time you were wrong about a technical decision and someone else was right.

sections.title: Candidate questions
sections.prompt: What questions do you have for us?

anchors.1: Style nits only, misses the main bug, or feedback is vague or harsh
anchors.2: Finds the obvious bug and one logic or validation gap, with specific and polite feedback
anchors.3: Finds them all, ranks by impact, catches a subtle issue, and the feedback explains why and teaches

anchors.2: Asks relevant questions, defines a first version
anchors.3: Questions change the scope, first version fits a small student team, names what is cut

anchors.2: Clear pieces, data flow and storage
anchors.3: Also names the API, a failure point, and a data or user concern (privacy, bad inputs)

anchors.2: Traces one data flow end to end
anchors.3: Explains tradeoffs, hardest bug, and what they would change

anchors.1: Hands out tasks, or vague "make them feel valued"
anchors.2: Concrete steps, such as owning a piece end to end or real input on decisions
anchors.3: Tailors to each person, builds real autonomy and growth, supports less experienced members

anchors.1: Hides the problem or cuts randomly
anchors.2: Cuts by priority and tells the team
anchors.3: Cuts by client impact, tells the PL and client early, offers a plan

anchors.2: Says "not sure" at times, uses hints
anchors.3: Reasons from a hint, owns gaps, adjusts mid answer

red_flags.text: Harsh or dismissive feedback to a member
Designs a full solution without asking a question
Can't explain their own code, or takes all the credit and names no mistakes
Hides the problem or cuts without telling anyone
States something wrong as fact instead of saying "not sure"
